items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: The interviewee discusses listening to recordings of Basie and Goodman, mentioning they are 'great artists' and listing personnel, but describes no personal interaction, meeting, or professional collaboration with Basie or Goodman himself.

ctx.x: It was awful. The tape that was made in the 70s especially. When you went back it just started shredding and you’d stop. So we were literally putting them in little ovens, and we called it baking the tapes to keep them from just flaking — you know if you ran it through one time it was gone. There was all the oxide laying on the table. So one of the guys got the idea that baking them — and now they do it — it’s very sophisticated. But I started listening — I was kind of skeptical when I saw those tapes and I put…

items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: I talk to my student about this is twelve years before Jackie Robinson and the Dodgers. And that’s my whole basis of my class is music played the bigger part of integrating society than the courts or baseball or something like that. So I knew Mr. Hammond, I knew the music...

ctx.x: When they cut those solos out then they were splicing tape?

Um hum. So what I was finding was the tape with the splicing, the splices. You know how they have the white splice tape of course. But they would cut right, diagonally. They were professionally edited. But on other reels I started hearing pieces of things. Or I’d hear one that was not edited. And I said I don’t remember that. And I’d start listening and I’d start making — I had tablets filled with notes. And then I started finding reels with — it was spliced but you’d start playing it and it would be like a solo,…

electric guitar and then that would go on for a while and there would be a splice and here’s another solo from a totally different song. It was just solos on these reels, spliced together. And I started listening and it doesn’t take a genius to figure out that’s Lester Young trading off of Charlie Christian. These things. I get chill bumps as you can imagine. So I started — I was literally, I don’t know how many legal pads I filled with notes on this. And I got with Doug Sax and started constructing this stuff.…
